q: How is the Jury for an ADC composed under SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.4.2?
o: Entirely of Registered and Licensed Architects, with no lay representation
A majority of laypersons chosen by the Owner, assisted by one Architect
An equal number of Architects and Engineers, with the Owner casting the tie-breaking vote
A majority of Registered and Licensed Architects (RLAs), assisted by a lay Juror who represents and voices the intention of the Owner
n: The Jury consists of a majority of Registered and Licensed Architects (RLAs), assisted by a lay Juror to represent and voice the intention of the Owner. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.4.2)

q: After winning an ADC, an architect discovers that the Owner has taken portions of her design plus portions of another Competitor's entry to compose a new, combined design, without either author's consent. Is this permitted under SPP Doc. 208?
o: No, but only because RA 8293 was violated — RA 9266 does not apply to this situation
No — the Owner or his agents are not free to pick out portions of entries to compose another plan/design; this requires the authors' agreement and is protected under RA 9266 and RA 8293
Yes, but only if the Owner is the awarding first-prize winner's direct employer
Yes, once prizes are paid, the Owner acquires full and unrestricted rights to alter or combine any entries
n: Sec. 13.6.7 expressly states that the Owner or his agents are not free to pick out portions of the entries to compose another plan/design; ADC-generated designs may not be used or altered except by agreement with the author, per the ownership/copyright provisions of RA 9266 and RA 8293. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.6.7)
scenario: An Owner combines portions of the winning entry with portions of another Competitor's entry to produce a new composite design, without securing either author's consent.

q: A budget for the Secretariat's salary in an ADC must be earmarked to cover what span of time?
o: Throughout the duration of the Competition, from the time it is launched up to the end of the Exhibition and Awarding
Only during the design/entry-submission phase, ending once entries are received
From the announcement of results up to one month after
Only during the actual day of Jury deliberation
n: A budget must be earmarked for the salary of the Secretariat throughout the duration of the Competition, from the time it is launched and up to the end of the Exhibition and Awarding. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.5.1)

q: A first-prize winner of a Project ADC is unable to satisfy the Jury of his ability to carry out the plan/design work. What may the Jury require under Sec. 13.6.8?
o: The Jury may automatically disqualify the winner and award the commission to the second-prize winner instead
The Owner may proceed to build the design without any Architect's further involvement
The winner may be required to collaborate with another Architect of the winning Competitor's own choice, duly approved by the Jury and the Owner
The winner forfeits the prize money entirely
n: If the winning Competitor is unable to satisfy the Jury of his ability to carry out the plan/design work, the Jury may require the winner to collaborate with another Architect of the winning Competitor's choice, duly approved by the Jury and Owner. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.6.8)
scenario: A first-prize winner of a Project ADC cannot convince the Jury that she has the capability to execute her own winning design.

q: Aside from Secretariat salary, what other cost item may the Competition Budget cover under Sec. 13.5.1.2?
o: Malpractice insurance for all participating architects
The construction cost of the winning design
The Owner's general corporate operating expenses
Office overhead cost, including office rental (if necessary), transportation, office supplies, and meals
n: A budget can also be earmarked for office overhead cost, including office rental (if necessary), transportation, office supplies, and meals. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.5.1.2)

q: A Project ADC announces its Jury's award on January 15. By January 15 of the following year, the Owner still has not signed a contract with the first-prize winner. Under SPP Doc. 208, what must happen, and does the Owner thereby gain the right to build the project without the winner?
o: The first prize must be returned by the winner to the Owner
The Owner is released from all further obligations and may build the project using any architect it chooses
The competition is automatically nullified and a new competition must be held
The winner must be compensated a further sum equal to the first prize amount, but the Owner still does not acquire the right to carry out the project except with the collaboration of the Author
n: If twelve (12) months pass after the announcement of the Jury's award with no contract signed, the Conditions must provide for the first-prize winner to receive a further sum equal to the first prize; but this compensation does not give the Owner the right to carry out the project except with the collaboration of its Author. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.6.9)
scenario: A Project ADC's Jury award is announced on January 15; twelve months later, the Owner still has not signed a contract with the first-prize winner.

q: How is the Technical Advisor compensated under SPP Doc. 208?
o: With free membership in the IAPOA
With a share of the prize money
With a monthly salary equal to the Secretariat's
With an Honorarium as a consultation fee
n: The Technical Advisor shall also be provided with an Honorarium as a Consultation Fee. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.5.3)

q: Broadly, Sec. 13 of SPP Doc. 208 (Architectural Design Competitions) organizes the ADC around which set of bodies/roles?
o: The Competition Secretariat, the Professional Advisor, Technical Advisors, and the Jury, together with the budget/cost items and prize/honoraria rules that govern them
The Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture acting as sole organizer and judge
A single Competition Director who performs all administrative, advisory, and judging functions alone
Only the Owner and the winning Competitor, with no other parties involved
n: Sec. 13 sets out the organizational structure of an ADC — the Competition Secretariat (13.1), Professional Advisor (13.2), Technical Advisors (13.3), and Jury (13.4) — plus the Competition Budget/Costs (13.5) and Prizes, Honoraria and Mentions (13.6) that fund and reward the process. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13)

q: An Owner is organizing an ADC and asks a Professional Practice consultant which budget items must be provided for. Which of the following items should the consultant tell the Owner to include?
o: Only the prizes for the winning entries; all advisory and secretariat work is rendered gratis
Only the Jurors' honorarium; the Professional and Technical Advisors are volunteers by default
A single consolidated fee equal to a percentage of the PCC covering everyone involved
Secretariat salary, office overhead costs, and honoraria for the Professional Advisor, Technical Advisor, and Jurors
n: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.5 requires a budget for the Secretariat's salary, office overhead costs, and honoraria for the Professional Advisor, the Technical Advisor (as a consultation fee), and the Jurors (covering the judging period, plus accommodation/food/transportation/airfare as needed). (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.5.1-13.5.4)

q: Across Sec. 13.5 (Budget/Costs) and Sec. 13.6 (Prizes/Honoraria/Mentions), which principle recurs regarding who bears the competition's financial obligations?
o: The IAPOA funds all honoraria and prizes on the Owner's behalf
Each Competitor is responsible for funding the Secretariat and Jury out of pocket

The Owner bears the Secretariat salary, overhead, and all advisors'/Jurors' honoraria and reimbursable expenses, and must also pay adequate prizes and honoraria to Competitors within the timelines set
Only the first-prize winner's expenses are reimbursed; all other costs are absorbed by the Professional Advisor personally
n: Throughout Sec. 13, the Owner is consistently the party responsible for funding the Secretariat's salary and overhead (13.5.1), the honoraria and reimbursable expenses of the Professional Advisor, Technical Advisor, and Jurors (13.5.2-13.5.4), and for paying adequate, appropriately-scaled prizes and honoraria to Competitors within the stated deadlines (13.6.1-13.6.6). (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.5, 13.6)

q: In an Ideas Competition (as opposed to a Project ADC), how may prize remuneration be limited under Sec. 13.6.2?
o: All entrants, win or lose, must receive equal remuneration
No remuneration whatsoever is allowed in an Ideas Competition
It may be possible to remunerate only the First Prize Winner
Only the Second and Third Prize winners may be remunerated
n: For an Ideas Competition only, it may be possible to remunerate only the first (1st) prize winner. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.6.2)

q: Which of the following is NOT listed as a possible member/component of the Competition Secretariat?
o: Encoder/Researcher
Technical Advisor
Support Staff/OJTs
Secretary/Receptionist
n: The Secretariat may include a Secretary/Receptionist (13.1.1), Encoder/Researcher (13.1.2), and Support Staff/OJTs (13.1.3). The Technical Advisor is a separate role (Sec. 13.3), a specialist consulted by the Jurors. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.1.1-13.1.3, 13.3)

q: Within what period must the Owner pay the prizes after the ADC results are officially announced?
o: Within six (6) months
Within one (1) month of the official announcement of the results
Within one (1) year
Within one (1) week
n: The Owner undertakes to accept the decisions of the Jury and to pay the prizes allotted within one (1) month of the official announcement of the ADC results. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.6.3)

q: Which of the following is part of the Professional Advisor's role under Sec. 13.2.2?
o: Casting the deciding vote when the Jury is deadlocked
Personally judging and ranking all competition entries
Fixing the amount of all prizes without Owner approval
Supervising the ADC timetable, receipt of Competitors' questions, dispatch of replies, receipt of entries, and safeguarding Competitors' anonymity, while preparing the Conditions
n: The Professional Advisor supervises the conduct of the ADC and prepares the Conditions, ensuring the timetable is followed, supervising receipt of Competitors' questions and dispatch of replies, receiving entries, and safeguarding the anonymity of Competitors at all times. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.2.2)

q: What additional benefit does each participant in a limited ADC by invitation receive under Sec. 13.6.4?
o: Automatic inclusion in the next competition's Jury
An honorarium, in addition to the prizes awarded
A guaranteed commission for a future project
Free membership in the IAPOA
n: Each participant in a limited ADC by invitation shall receive an honorarium in addition to the prizes awarded. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.6.4)

q: The Professional Advisor's responsibilities under SPP Doc. 208 are limited to which scope?
o: The financial audit of the Owner's overall project budget
The licensing and accreditation of participating architects
The organization and the conduct of the competition
The construction supervision of the winning design
n: Sec. 13.2.4 states that the Professional Advisor's responsibilities are limited to the organization and the conduct of the competition. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.2.4)

q: A two-stage ADC narrows 20 first-stage entries down to 5 qualifiers for the second stage. Under SPP Doc. 208, what must the Owner do for these 5 qualifiers?
o: Pay them nothing until the final results are announced
Pay each of them a reasonable honorarium, stated in the Conditions, to reimburse the additional second-stage work, on top of whatever prizes are eventually awarded
Require them to forfeit any right to a later prize in exchange for advancing to the second stage
Automatically award each of them a Jury seat for the second stage
n: Sec. 13.6.5-13.6.6 requires a reasonable honorarium to be paid to each Competitor selected for the second stage, to reimburse the additional work of that stage; this is stated in the Conditions and is separate from and in addition to the prizes eventually awarded. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.6.5-13.6.6)
scenario: A two-stage ADC narrows 20 first-stage entries down to 5 qualifiers who are invited to develop full second-stage submissions.

q: Who appoints the Jury in an Architectural Design Competition, and who are its members called?
o: The Jury is appointed by the Owner to assess the competition entries; its members are called Jurors
The Jury is appointed by the IAPOA alone, without Owner involvement; its members are called Examiners
The Jury is appointed by the Professional Advisor; its members are called Assessors
The Jury is elected by the Competitors themselves; its members are called Panelists
n: The Jury is composed of the people appointed by the Owner to assess the entries to the competition, and the members of the Jury are called Jurors. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.4.1)

q: The restriction against using or altering an ADC-generated design without the author's agreement is covered by which laws under Sec. 13.6.7?
o: R.A. No. 6541 (National Building Code) only
Secs. 20(4) and 33 of R.A. No. 9266 (The Architecture Act of 2004) and R.A. No. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines), with their IRRs
Presidential Decree No. 1096 alone
R.A. No. 386 (Civil Code of the Philippines) exclusively
n: This restriction on the use/alteration of ADC-generated plans/designs is covered by applicable ownership and copyright provisions under Secs. 20(4) and 33 of R.A. No. 9266 (The Architecture Act of 2004) and of R.A. No. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) and their respective Implementing Rules and Regulations. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.6.7; RA 9266 Secs. 20(4) & 33; RA 8293)

q: Who nominates the Jurors, and who approves the nomination?
o: Jurors are nominated by the Owner and approved by the Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects (IAPOA)
Jurors are self-nominated and approved by the Competition Secretariat
Jurors are nominated by the Professional Advisor and approved by the Owner
Jurors are nominated by the IAPOA and approved by the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC)
n: Jurors are nominated by the Owner and approved by the Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects (IAPOA). (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.4.3)

q: In a Project ADC, what obligation does the award of first prize to a plan/design place on the Owner, under Sec. 13.6.8?
o: An obligation to immediately begin construction within 30 days
No obligation beyond payment of the prize money
An obligation to entrust the Author of the winning plan/design with the commission for the Project
An obligation to make the Author a permanent employee of the Owner's organization
n: In Project ADCs, the award of first prize to a plan/design places the Owner under an obligation to entrust the Author of the plan/design with the commission for the Project. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.6.8)

q: How may Secretariat salaries be structured under Sec. 13.5.1.1?
o: A monthly basis for the temporary staff, and a weekly allowance for support staff such as OJTs who assist in the Judging, Exhibit, and Awarding ceremonies
A percentage of the total prize money awarded
A single lump-sum payment made only after the Awarding ceremony
A daily wage for all Secretariat members without distinction
n: Salary can be on a monthly basis for the temporary staff, and a weekly allowance for support staff like OJTs who assist in the Judging, Exhibit, and Awarding ceremonies. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.5.1.1)

q: In a Project ADC, if no contract is signed with the first-prize winner within twelve (12) months of the announcement of the Jury's award, what must the Conditions provide for under Sec. 13.6.9?
o: Automatic transfer of the commission to the second-prize winner
Compensation to the first-prize winner of a further sum equal to the amount of the first prize
A doubling of the honorarium paid to the Jurors
Automatic forfeiture of the first prize already paid
n: Provisions shall be made in the ADC Conditions for the first prize winner to receive compensation of a further sum equal to the amount of the first prize if no contract is signed within twelve (12) months of the announcement of the Jury's award. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.6.9)

q: What compensation and reimbursement is the Professional Advisor entitled to under Sec. 13.5.2?
o: No honorarium, only reimbursement of out-of-pocket transportation expenses
A percentage of the Project/Construction Cost (PCC), similar to comprehensive architectural services
An Honorarium per month during the duration of the Competition, plus Owner-reimbursed expenses for board and lodging, transportation, and airfare if travel is required
A single flat honorarium paid only once, at the end of the competition, with no reimbursements
n: The Professional Advisor shall be provided with an Honorarium per month during the duration of the Competition. Expenses for board and lodging, transportation, and airfare, if travel for the Advisor is so required, shall be reimbursed by the Owner. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.5.2)

q: In an Ideas Competition, if the Owner later decides to make use of all or part of the winning scheme, what must the Owner do?
o: Do so with the collaboration of the Author, on terms of collaboration acceptable to the Author
Proceed freely, since Ideas Competitions carry no author's-rights restriction
Obtain approval solely from the Jury, without involving the Author at all
Pay only an additional flat fee, without needing the Author's collaboration or consent to terms
n: In an Ideas Competition, if the Owner decides to make use of all or part of the winning scheme, he should do so with the collaboration of the Author, and the terms of collaboration must be acceptable to the Author. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.6 (final provision))

q: What must the Jurors' Honorarium cover under Sec. 13.5.4?
o: The period for the Judging, with expenses for accommodation, food, transportation, and airfare also charged to the Owner
Only a token gift with no cash compensation
A fixed percentage of the total prize fund
The Jurors' travel expenses only, with no honorarium for their judging work
n: The Jurors shall also be provided with an Honorarium to cover the period for the Judging. Expenses for accommodation, food, transportation, and airfare shall also be on the account of the Owner. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.5.4)

q: Which statement correctly distinguishes the roles of the Professional Advisor and the Jury in an ADC?
o: The Professional Advisor votes on the winning entry, while the Jury only handles administrative paperwork
The Professional Advisor organizes and administers the competition and assists the Jury without voting, while the Jury (majority RLAs plus a lay Juror) actually assesses and decides on the entries
The Jury handles all administrative matters, while the Professional Advisor judges and ranks the entries
The Professional Advisor and the Jury are the same body under a different name
n: The Professional Advisor organizes and supervises the ADC's conduct, prepares the Conditions, and assists the Jury during deliberations without a vote (Sec. 13.2), while the Jury — a majority of RLAs assisted by a lay Juror representing the Owner — is the body that actually assesses the entries and decides the results (Sec. 13.4). (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.2, 13.4)

q: Under Sec. 13.6.1, what must the prizes awarded in an ADC be related to?
o: The number of entries submitted in the competition
The size and complexity of the project, the amount of work involved, and the expense incurred by the Competitors
The number of years of experience of the Owner's staff
The market value of the land on which the project will be built
n: The prizes awarded must be related to the size and complexity of the project, the amount of work involved, and the expense incurred by Competitors; it is important for the Owner to allot adequate prize money to compensate all Competitors for their work. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.6.1)

q: What is the Competition Secretariat under an Architectural Design Competition (ADC)?
o: The body formed by the Owner and approved by the Professional Advisor to assist the Professional Advisor and the Jury in the administrative conduct of the ADC
The group of specialists consulted by the Jurors for technical information
The Owner's legal counsel who drafts the Conditions of the competition
The panel of registered and licensed architects who judge the entries
n: The Competition Secretariat is the body formed by the Owner and approved by the Professional Advisor, tasked with assisting the Professional Advisor and the Jury in the administrative conduct of the ADC. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.1)

q: An Owner is organizing an Ideas Competition for a conceptual master plan and wants to minimize the remuneration budget. Under SPP Doc. 208, what is the minimum the Owner may lawfully remunerate?
o: Only the Jurors, not the Competitors
Only the First Prize Winner, since Sec. 13.6.2 allows remuneration to be limited to the first prize in an Ideas Competition
Every entrant equally, regardless of ranking
Nothing at all, since Ideas Competitions carry no obligation to pay any prize
n: Sec. 13.6.2 specifically allows an Ideas Competition to remunerate only the First Prize Winner, distinguishing it from Project ADCs where broader compensation obligations (e.g., Sec. 13.6.1's adequate-compensation principle) generally apply. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.6.2)

q: Under SPP Doc. 208, who nominates/appoints and pays the Professional Advisor of an ADC, and who approves that appointment?
o: The Owner nominates, appoints, and pays the Professional Advisor; the IAPOA National Board of Directors (NBD), through its ADC Committee, approves the appointment
The Competition Secretariat nominates the Professional Advisor, subject to Owner approval only
The Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture appoints and pays the Professional Advisor
The Jury nominates and pays the Professional Advisor; the Owner approves
n: The Professional Advisor is an Architect nominated/appointed and paid by the Owner, and approved by the IAPOA National Board of Directors (NBD) through its ADC Committee, to organize the ADC on the Owner's behalf. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.2.1)

q: The results of an ADC are officially announced on March 1. Under SPP Doc. 208, by what date must the Owner have paid the allotted prizes?
o: On or before March 8 (within one week)
On or before September 1 (within six months)
On or before April 1 (within one month of the announcement)
There is no deadline; payment may be made at the Owner's discretion
n: Sec. 13.6.3 obligates the Owner to accept the Jury's decisions and pay the prizes within one (1) month of the official announcement of the ADC results — i.e., by April 1 if results were announced March 1. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.6.3)
scenario: An ADC's results are officially announced on March 1.

q: During Jury deliberations, what is the role of the Professional Advisor?
o: He votes only in case of a tie among Jurors
He is excluded from all Jury deliberations to preserve independence
He chairs the Jury and casts the final deciding vote
He assists the Jury and is present during deliberations, but has no vote
n: The Professional Advisor will assist the Jury and be present during its deliberations, but he will have no vote. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.2.3)

q: In a two-stage ADC, what is paid to Competitors who are selected to proceed to the second stage?
o: A reasonable honorarium, in addition to the prizes awarded, to reimburse them for the additional work of the second stage, as stated in the Conditions
A refund of their first-stage entry fee only
Nothing, since only the final winner is compensated
The full first-prize amount, paid in advance
n: In two-stage competitions, a reasonable honorarium shall be paid to each of the Competitors selected to take part in the second stage. This sum reimburses them for the additional work carried out in the second stage, is stated in the Conditions, and is in addition to the prizes awarded. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.6.5-13.6.6)

q: What is the function of Technical Advisors in an ADC?
o: They prepare and finalize the competition Conditions in place of the Professional Advisor
They are appointed to represent the Owner's interest in place of the lay Juror
They vote alongside the Jurors on the winning entry
They are specialist personnel who may be consulted by the Jurors during the conduct of the ADC to permit them to obtain all necessary relevant information
n: Technical Advisors are Specialist personnel who may be consulted by the Jurors during the conduct of the ADC to permit them to obtain all necessary relevant information. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.3)

q: What must the Conditions of an ADC state regarding the winning plan/design, and what restriction applies to its use under Sec. 13.6.7?
o: The Owner may combine portions of several entries into a new design without the authors' consent, provided prizes were paid
The winning design automatically becomes public domain upon announcement of results
The Conditions must state the use to which the Owner will put the winning design; the design may not be used or altered in any way except by agreement with the author
The Conditions need not mention the intended use; the Owner may use or alter the design freely once prizes are paid
n: The Conditions shall state the use to which the Owner will put the winning plan/design. ADC-generated plans/designs may not be used or altered in any way except by agreement with the author, and the Owner or his agents are not free to pick out portions of entries to compose another plan/design. (Source: SPP Doc. 208, Sec. 13.6.7)
